memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
Then the LORD said to Moses: "Take the blasphemer outside the camp. All
those who heard him are to lay their hands on his head, and the entire
assembly is to stone him" - Lev 24:13-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a difficult passage and we should not rush past its weight. A
man is taken outside the camp and executed by the whole community. Those
who heard the blasphemy laid hands on his head, formally testifying to
what they had witnessed.

Let us be clear about what this was. Israel was a nation under a
covenant, and this was its civil and criminal law, given at a specific
point in redemptive history. It was never given to the church as a
pattern for how believers should treat blasphemers today. Jesus
explicitly refused to let His disciples call down fire on those who
rejected Him (Luke 9:54-55).

But we should let the passage do its proper work. It tells us that God's
name is not a trivial thing. We live in a culture where God's name is
used as casual punctuation, and we barely flinch. Israel flinched.

Now look where the man was taken: outside the camp. Hebrews says Jesus
also suffered outside the city gate, and calls us to go to Him there,
bearing the disgrace He bore (Heb 13:12-13).

Consider the wonder of that. Jesus was condemned for blasphemy by the
high priest (Matt 26:65-66) — the sinless One, treated as the guilty
one, carried outside the camp so that guilty people could be brought in.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I grown casual about how God's name is used, including by me?
2. What does it mean that Jesus was condemned as a blasphemer in my
   place?
3. How does the cross hold both God's justice and His mercy together?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Holy God, Your name is precious. Forgive me for treating it lightly, and
thank You that Jesus was taken outside the camp so that I could be
welcomed in. Amen.
